**EDIT: this turned into a wall of text so...TL;DR:** The GOP might be manufacturing the internal, anti-Trump sentiment on purpose to astro-turf an anti-establishment movement; like with the Tea Party (which was also astro turfed). This would put their front runner in a better position to lure anti-establishment Democrats away from voting for Hillary.

Here's a thought: what if the GOP knows that it is getting out of touch with most Americans? What if they decided that their candidate needed to have a "revolutionary" appeal? What better way to approach this goal than to sacrifice a few lame ducks by having them run against him? By having many of the establishment GOP types speak out against Trump, publicly; and making feeble attempts to block his candidacy; they are actually strengthening his position. It is working so well, that it might be contrived. And the manufactured internal struggle, televised to a large audience, between imaginary and opposed internal Republican members, sets up a narrative that is very appealing to the US psychology.

I know it sounds a bit over the top, but think about it. "Everybody loves and underdog" is said frequently; but the truth is that it's more complicated. Everybody loves and underdog that wins; nobody likes and underdog that loses. Since Trump was already leading in the polls and the primaries, he was in a good position to become a messiah figure to the US populace. He'll beat down the establishment, he'll make America great again, he can't be bought; and all you gotta do in return is vote for him!

Astro-turfing a movement is not a new strategy for the GOP. The Tea Party was a very successful movement; one that appeared to be a grass roots movement, but was actually funded by the GOP establishment/lobbyists. Both the GOP and the Democrats have a recent history of trying to obfuscate political ties to big money, big oil, big whatever. This Trump phenomenon, to me anyway, seems to be getting a lot of traction in the press. Like, way more than you'd expect, and negative - even from the GOP. America may be seeing the anti-establishment astro-turfed movement unfolding right before their eyes. But is it true?

Hillary looks like she will secure the Democratic candidacy for president, and it doesn't get any more establishment than her. She's in bed with the banks and she has no problem selling herself to the public, she is definitely a skilled politician. And anyone who thinks she would be held to the same standard as us regular folks, for her email improprieties, is just as delusional as anyone who thought that George W. Bush would be held responsible for starting a war based on wrong intel. It doesn't matter if either of them were guilty of breaking laws that would send most of us to prison for a great many years; these people are effectively above the law.

So, how does the GOP fight against the first real shot some has at the first female president? Well, you have to take voters away from the Democrats. It doesn't take a rocket scientist to see that the Democrats are flocking to Sanders for the exact same reasons as Republicans are flocking toward Trump. People are sick and tired of seeing their country bought and sold at the political level, and so blatantly. So, with a imminent Hillary being propped up against Sanders for the Democrats, the Republicans are pulling potential Democrat voters to the GOP. I doubt that you'd see the same migration of Republicans, if Sanders gets the Dems candidacy.

Anyway, this is just another of my overly paranoid, what job theories, but it makes sense. If I'm wrong, then I am worried for America. I'm worried because, so many people are terrified of a Trump presidency. Maybe it's because of the end of the gravy train made possible by the politician / lobbyist relationship. But maybe it's because, instead of making America great, Trump might just be the first nail in the coffin for the American Empire. Either way, the upcoming American Presidential election will be interesting to watch; and the only thing we *can* be certain about, is that it *will* be watched...with lots of popcorn.
